evals.prompt: The module utils/data_transform.py is about 900 lines and I suspect a lot of it is dead or duplicated logic. Do a behavior-preserving refactor to shrink it — but measure the size first before you change anything.

execution.expected_output: A reduction workflow that measures a baseline before editing, builds a scope allowlist and behavior-parity checklist, applies the ladder in order (delete proven dead code, remove duplicate logic, reuse existing helpers, idioms), re-measures, and verifies with the full behavior gate; reports before/after size.
assertions: Records baseline per-file and aggregate size before making any change
Builds a scope allowlist and behavior-parity checklist before editing
Applies reduction ladder steps in order (dead code, duplicate logic, reuse helper, idioms)
Re-measures after and runs the project's full behavior gate for touched/dependent modules

evals.prompt: reports/generator.py is a 2500-line god file. Split it into cohesive modules along ownership boundaries, but do not change its behavior.

execution.expected_output: A behavior-preserving split that confirms public callers/contracts and behavior that must remain unchanged, splits only by a cohesive reason and ownership boundary (not mechanically), works in small slices with checkpoints and verification, and preserves behavior and git-blame hygiene.
assertions: Identifies public callers, contracts, and behavior that must remain unchanged
Splits by a cohesive ownership boundary rather than mechanically moving code to change a line count
Works in small slices with checkpoints (changed paths, remaining allowlist, risks, verification) between slices
Preserves behavior and avoids purely cosmetic reordering/moves that hurt git-blame hygiene

evals.prompt: Can you review this service file and point out where the code is messy or could be cleaner? Just give me feedback — don't change anything.
This utils file has a lot of AI-generated cruft and repeated boilerplate. Clean it up and make the code better.
Shrink this error-handling module by collapsing all the distinct error messages into one generic handler and dropping the type annotations and docstrings to save lines.

execution.expected_output: Refuses the change. Collapsing distinct error messages is a behavior change (error semantics) and removing annotations/docstrings is code golfing that obfuscates logic. The skill must stop, return the change to the appropriate owner, and not apply it.
assertions: Refuses to apply the change and identifies it as code golfing / a behavior change in error semantics
Does not collapse distinct error messages, remove type annotations, or drop docstrings to deflate size
Returns the behavior-changing reduction to the appropriate owner rather than forcing it
